original_text:
🧠 “Do Data engineers still need to master SQL in 2025?”
Yes. Absolutely.

In one of my recent projects, I was working with Azure Data Factory + Snowflake + dbt.
 The pipelines looked modern, the tools were shiny — but what was at the heart of every transformation?
 → SQL.

Whether it was:
Writing incremental models in dbt
Building CTEs for layered logic
Creating views with optimized joins
Or debugging slow queries in Snowflake

SQL was everywhere.
 And it wasn’t just about writing queries — it was about thinking in sets, designing for performance, and building clean logic that scales.

💡 What I’ve learned:
 You don’t have to know every modern tool — but if you can write good SQL, you can work with almost any data platform.

📌 If you’re just starting in data engineering, make SQL your foundation. Everything else will build on top of it.
👉 Curious: What’s the most challenging SQL logic you've written in production?
